## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels on this repository; suggested: `orig-external`, `cat-bugfix`, `mod-frost`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

`conv/frost/engine.py::_check_sm100` raised `NotImplementedError("frost_conv requires SM100, but found 103")` on a B300. The conv tests gate on `100 <= SM < 120` (`conv/frost/utils.py::requires_sm100`), so on cc 10.3 they ran and failed: no engine proposed a plan, or the gate raised.

The gate now accepts 100 and 103. The SM100-family conv templates (`templates/sm100_conv.py`, `templates/sm100_block_scale_conv.py`) compiled with `options="--enable-tvm-ffi"` only, so CuTe DSL picked the target, and they cached the artifact by shape, tile and epilogue alone. With both parts admitted, a process that built a convolution on SM100 would get that SM100 launchable back for the same graph on SM103. So:

- `_cutedsl.build_target()` names the build device (`cudnn.frost.device.current_device()`, the handle's inside `build_plan`) and its target: `sm_100a` on cc 10.0, `sm_103a` on cc 10.3.
- Both templates key their compile cache on that pair, and compile under that device's context with an explicit `--gpu-arch`. The dense `compile` resolves the pair and calls a cached `_compile_cached`.
- `test_block_scale_compiler_cache_keys_on_the_build_device` and `test_dense_compiler_cache_keys_on_the_build_device` model an SM100 and an SM103 GPU in both orders, with `cute.compile` recorded.

## Why

cc 10.3 runs the same templates; only the gate refused it.

## Related issues

None found.

## API and compatibility impact

None on cc 10.0. On cc 10.3, FROST conv graphs are now planned instead of declined.

## Testing

B300 (cc 10.3), develop `64ed3dfe` with its own extension, torch 2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.27.0, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, run from `test/python`:

| `python -m pytest -m "L0 or L1" conv/frost` | develop | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_block_scale_conv.py` | 43 failed | 43 passed |
| `test_conv_mode.py` | 3 failed, 3 skipped | 3 passed, 3 skipped |
| `test_conv_tile_config.py` | 55 passed, 6 skipped | 57 passed, 8 skipped |
| `test_conv_cutedsl_version_gate.py` | 5 passed | 5 passed |
| total | 46 failed, 60 passed, 86 skipped | 108 passed, 88 skipped |

`test_conv_tile_config.py` gains the two device-order cases of each new cache test. The 88 skips are the dense-conv cases, the new dense cache test among them, which need CuTe DSL >= 4.9; PyPI's latest release is 4.8.1, so I could not run them. Not run on cc 10.0, where the gate admits the part as before.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `d4099860e9dd` against base `f78022abad7b`.

Thank you for your contribution! The gate enables the existing SM100-family convolution path on SM103. Single-device SM100 checks passed. One P2 remains for reuse across SM100 and SM103 devices.

**[P2] Keep convolution compile caches separate across devices** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d4099860e9dd435c509a1b44e0e04dd6e3066138/python/cudnn/conv/frost/engine.py#L123))

After building an NVFP4 convolution on SM100, building the same graph on the newly accepted SM103 device can return the SM100 launchable. `sm100_block_scale_conv._compile_cached` keys shapes, tile and epilogue but omits device/target; the dense template's `compile` cache has the same omission. `build_plan` labels the returned plan with the new device, so the execute-time device check cannot detect that its compiled artifact belongs to the previous device. A probe retaining the real graph analysis, builder and block-scale cache compiled only once in both 100→103→100 and 103→100→103 sequences; clearing the cache compiled for the requested device. This exposes an existing cache omission through the wider gate. Include the resolved device/target in cache identity, or delegate reuse to the device-aware compiler cache, and test both device orders.

Evidence: probe-device-cache.py/log: real graph, support check, build_plan and template lru_cache; only device facts and final cute.compile boundary modeled. Plans record requested ordinal but reuse first artifact. Baseline gate rejects103; cold-cache control selects103. Templates unchanged from merge base. No foreign-device binary executed. Attribution: Existing argument-only cache omission exposed by newly accepting SM103.

Validation: Native SM100, exact Python source, CuTe DSL 4.8.0: convolution L0/L1 suite passed 106 tests; 86 dense-convolution cases skipped because they require DSL 4.9; 41 higher-level cases were deselected. A native NVFP4-to-BF16 convolution matched its reference, remained bitwise equal across five repeated runs, and matched the updated reference after input-scale changes and CUDA Graph replay with an explicitly bound handle stream. Modeled-device probes retained the real graph/build/cache path and checked both device orders, cold-cache controls and baseline/head architecture admission. These establish the cache decision, not native SM103 execution. Requested python/conv CI for this head; results are pending.

Limitations: No independent native SM103 run or mixed-device kernel launch was available. The author's B300 results are separate evidence. Dense convolution execution requires a newer DSL than the local 4.8.0 installation. No SM103 performance claim is made.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

Validation: Native SM100 with DSL 4.8.0: 108 convolution L0/L1 tests passed; 88 dense-path cases skipped because they require DSL 4.9; 41 higher-level cases were deselected. Independent block-scale probe retained the real graph analysis, build_plan, template preparation and cache. Both SM100/SM103 orders and two SM100 devices compiled once per device, reused their own artifacts, selected the expected explicit target, and restored the modeled context. The dense template's real preparation/cache functions passed the same three device sequences with the compiler leaf modeled. Its occupancy query ran inside the requested device context, once per cold device build. The incremental change is confined to host compilation/cache identity, target selection and tests. Kernel bodies, arithmetic order, launch geometry and execute-time behavior are unchanged. Precheck found no candidates. Requested python/conv CI for this head. The prior pipeline passed on the earlier revision; it is not current-head validation.

Limitations: No physical mixed-GPU or native SM103 execution was available. Device facts, context switching and the compiler leaf were modeled in the cross-device probes; no foreign-target binary was launched. Dense compilation and execution on DSL 4.9 remain untested locally. The host cache probe does not replace that coverage. CI is pending.

Comment only: this PR already has an active approval; preserving existing approvals.

@@ -31,4 +31,19 @@ def requirement_error(what: str, minimum_version: tuple[int, int]) -> str | None
     return f"{what} requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= {floor}; found {raw_version}. " f"Upgrade with: pip install -U 'nvidia-cutlass-dsl>={floor}'"
 
 
-__all__ = ["BLOCK_SCALE_CUTEDSL_MIN_VERSION", "DENSE_CUTEDSL_MIN_VERSION", "requirement_error"]
+_SM100_FAMILY_TARGETS = {(10, 0): "sm_100a", (10, 3): "sm_103a"}
+
+
+def build_target() -> tuple[int, str]:
+    """The device a convolution built now targets (the handle's, inside ``build_plan``) and its CuTe target.
+
+    A compiled convolution belongs to that device: its arch-specific cubin, the max active clusters it bakes in and the
+    context it loads into. Both values therefore join every compile-cache key, and the compile runs under that device's
+    context with an explicit ``--gpu-arch``. A part outside the SM100 family (the engine declines it) reads as ``sm_100a``."""
+    from cudnn.frost.device import compute_capability, current_device
+
+    device = current_device()
+    return device, _SM100_FAMILY_TARGETS.get(tuple(compute_capability(device)), "sm_100a")
+
+
+__all__ = ["BLOCK_SCALE_CUTEDSL_MIN_VERSION", "DENSE_CUTEDSL_MIN_VERSION", "build_target", "requirement_error"]

-    if sm != 100:
-        raise NotImplementedError(f"frost_conv requires SM100, but found {sm}")

Thanks. Fixed in 102fe0c5 (the [P2] convolution compile caches across devices):

- `_cutedsl.build_target()` names the build device (`cudnn.frost.device.current_device()`, the handle's inside `build_plan`) and its target: `sm_100a` on cc 10.0, `sm_103a` on cc 10.3.

  - the dense `compile` now resolves them and calls a cached `_compile_cached`.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `d4099860e9dd` against base `f78022abad7b`.

Thank you for your contribution! The gate enables the existing SM100-family convolution path on SM103. Single-device SM100 checks passed. One P2 remains for reuse across SM100 and SM103 devices.

**[P2] Keep convolution compile caches separate across devices** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d4099860e9dd435c509a1b44e0e04dd6e3066138/python/cudnn/conv/frost/engine.py#L123))

After building an NVFP4 convolution on SM100, building the same graph on the newly accepted SM103 device can return the SM100 launchable. `sm100_block_scale_conv._compile_cached` keys shapes, tile and epilogue but omits device/target; the dense template's `compile` cache has the same omission. `build_plan` labels the returned plan with the new device, so the execute-time device check cannot detect that its compiled artifact belongs to the previous device. A probe retaining the real graph analysis, builder and block-scale cache compiled only once in both 100→103→100 and 103→100→103 sequences; clearing the cache compiled for the requested device. This exposes an existing cache omission through the wider gate. Include the resolved device/target in cache identity, or delegate reuse to the device-aware compiler cache, and test both device orders.

Evidence: probe-device-cache.py/log: real graph, support check, build_plan and template lru_cache; only device facts and final cute.compile boundary modeled.
